clue.text: Chief shortly to pin decoration on chest

indicators.note: shortly means the word for chief is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the boss is the chief
OM is the Order of Merit, a British decoration

explanation.surface: A leader is about to fix a medal on someone's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the final letter of the word for chief; 'pin' and 'on' merely join the pieces, so the decoration follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosom is the breast, a straightforward synonym for the chest.

clue.text: Finch seen by bishop out walking

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rambling is walking for pleasure in the country

explanation.surface: A small bird is spotted by a clergyman on a country walk.
explanation.definitionFit: The brambling is a species of finch from northern Europe, an example of the family.

clue.text: Finally abandoned Greek island for a Pacific group

indicators.note: the island's final letter is abandoned, dropped from the end

parts.note: Samos is an island in the Aegean

explanation.surface: A Greek island was ultimately given up in favour of a Pacific archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: SAMOS loses its last letter to give SAMO, and then the clue's 'a' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an island group in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Novelist married, then he tried for break-up

indicators.note: a break-up scatters these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer wed, and then her husband sought a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: George Meredith was a Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: George Meredith wrote novels such as The Egoist, so he is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Preparing to set limb, rubbing oil in

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a wing is a bird's limb
esters are the fragrant compounds in oils such as wintergreen used for rubbing

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to set a broken limb massages oil into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preparing to set' is said of the sun sinking towards the west, not of a bone being set.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun moving towards the west is about to go down, so westering describes it preparing to set.

clue.text: Socialist family toils on book

parts.note: toils are a net or snare, as in caught in the toils, so a web

explanation.surface: A left-wing household labours over a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toils' looks like a verb but is the noun for a snare. Sidney and Beatrice Webb were Fabian socialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney and Beatrice Webb were a married pair of leading Fabian socialists.

clue.text: Still leading a charmed existence?

definitions.meaning: living under a magic charm, bound by a spell

explanation.definitionFit: One who is held motionless by wonder is rapt; literally, one under an enchantment is held by magic.

clue.text: Record farm animal around northern forest

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: around means the animal word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A recording made of a pig circling in a northern wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Epping Forest is an ancient woodland on London's north-east edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Epping is the name of a well-known forest in Essex, an example of the word.

clue.text: Perform what's somewhat simple, mentally

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: To carry out what is, in a way, mentally simple.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Perform what's' as the definition; only 'Perform' defines the verb, and 'what's' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To implement a plan is to carry it out, a synonym of perform.

clue.text: No end of hazard, putting last of alcohol in tincture

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the shortened word
no end of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to hazard is to guess, as in hazard a guess

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dangerous amount of drink being added to a medicinal tincture.
explanation.walkthrough: GUESS loses its end to give GUES, and L, the last letter of alcohol, goes inside. 'tincture' here is a heraldic colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a tincture is a colour or metal, and gules is the name for red.

clue.text: Excellent farmland for investing a little foreign cash

indicators.note: investing means wrapping round, so the farmland word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: arable land is farmland used for crops
DM is the abbreviation for the Deutschmark, a former foreign currency
a is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Fine farmland, good for putting a bit of overseas money into.
explanation.walkthrough: The Deutschmark was Germany's currency before the euro; 'for investing' means the farmland word wraps round the cash and the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something admirable deserves praise, so the word serves as a synonym for excellent.

clue.text: Schoolboy returned impudence revolting

indicators.note: returned says the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, impudence
up as in up in arms, in revolt

explanation.surface: A pupil answers back insolently and rebelliously.
explanation.walkthrough: LIP followed by UP gives LIPUP, which read backwards yields the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a child at school, so a schoolboy is one example of the word.

clue.text: Strong liquor gets bachelor excited

parts.note: randy means sexually excited

explanation.surface: Hard drink makes an unmarried man amorous.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a distilled spirit, an example of strong liquor.

clue.text: Waterfowl catching onset of Lyme disease

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: ganders are male geese, waterfowl

indicators.note: onset of picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Geese pick up Lyme disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts L, the first letter of Lyme, inside GANDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Glanders is a contagious bacterial infection of horses, so it is a disease.

clue.text: Popularity of this show is taking off

definitions.text: Popularity of this show is taking off

parts.words: Popularity of this show is taking off
parts.note: taking off reads as becoming popular, but here means removing clothes, which is the show's whole act

explanation.definitionFit: The appeal of a burlesque undressing act lies in performers removing their clothing.

clue.text: Taxation system in which one gets small coin in change

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in places the coin inside the word for change

parts.note: a mutation is a change
P stands for a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: A tax regime under which someone receives a little coin as change.
explanation.walkthrough: I is followed by MUTATION with P slipped in after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Imputation is a system of company taxation crediting tax already paid by the company to shareholders.

clue.text: Description of Oedipus is capital, I'd heard

indicators.note: heard signals that the words are spoken and give a different spelling

parts.note: Paris is a capital city, followed by the clue's I'd

explanation.surface: Oedipus is described in a capital, I'd heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Oedipus killed his father Laius, so he fits the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A parricide is someone who kills a parent, as Oedipus killed his father.

clue.text: Catcalls from the house

parts.note: read literally, these are the cries of a house cat, not jeers from an audience; the word also names a row of houses

explanation.definitionFit: A cat's cry is a mew, so a domestic cat's cries are this plural; the word also means a street of converted stables.

clue.text: One preparing for explosion in boring game

parts.note: slow can mean dull or boring
a match is a game

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready for an outburst during a tedious fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow match is a fuse cord that burns steadily to set off an explosive charge.

clue.text: Cleverly avoiding cold by keeping warm

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
heating means keeping warm

explanation.surface: Smartly dodging a chill by staying warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating, as in cheating death, means escaping something by skill or luck.

clue.text: Maybe gruesome train service? Travel in first!

parts.note: to go is to travel
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A dreadful rail service, where you must go first class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travel in first!' tells you the travel word comes before the railway; 'Maybe' marks the answer as one instance of gruesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Gory means bloody and horrible, a near synonym of gruesome.

clue.text: Intended keeping husband, rejecting outrageous manoeuvre by bishop

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: an intended is a fiancé

indicators.note: rejecting turns the next piece back on itself

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means outrageous

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be holds on to her husband while refusing some wild scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop' is the chess piece, and the manoeuvre is a standard chess opening move; 'rejecting' turns the word for outrageous back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, a fianchetto develops a bishop onto the long diagonal next to the castled side.

clue.text: She has mate tailed at length, employing a number of eyes

definitions.text: She has mate tailed at length, employing a number of eyes

parts.words: She has mate tailed at length, employing a number of eyes
parts.note: a female bird whose partner has a very long tail decorated with many eye-like spots

explanation.definitionFit: The female of the peafowl is paired with the peacock, whose long train carries many eyespots.

clue.text: One may have a stab translating T S Eliot — about time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
translating means changing into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries rendering T S Eliot into another language, against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translating' makes STILETO from TSELIOT; 'about' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a slim dagger, the thing that makes a stab.

clue.text: Season with no new growth on branch

indicators.note: with no means the following letter is removed

parts.note: spring is a season

explanation.surface: A season without fresh shoots on the bough.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig growing on a branch.

clue.text: Has chap permission to join motorway chaos?

parts.note: may expresses permission, as in you may go
he refers to a chap
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Is the man allowed on the motorway, or will it cause havoc?
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder, a synonym for chaos.

clue.text: It may be spotted in hard currency area

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: A thing that could be noticed in the hard-currency zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' means having spots, as the spotted hyena does, not seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is a well-known species, so the animal may be spotted.

clue.text: Jazz-singing son gains fan

parts.note: a cat, or hep cat, was jazz slang for a fan

explanation.surface: A boy picks up an admirer of his jazz vocals.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is improvised jazz singing using nonsense syllables.

clue.text: Memorial flowers said to be for Auntie's old boss

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken and we hear a different spelling

parts.note: a wreath is a ring of flowers laid in memory of someone

explanation.surface: Funeral flowers are claimed to be meant for an aunt's former employer.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC; Lord Reith was its first director-general.
explanation.definitionFit: John Reith founded and first ran the BBC, the broadcaster nicknamed Auntie.

clue.text: Designer modified her tactic

indicators.note: modified means altered, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A planner changed her strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect designs buildings, so a designer is an apt synonym.

clue.text: Certified judo practitioner protected lung

definitions.meaning: a judoka graded with a coloured belt of a certain level
land around a city kept from building, serving as its breathing space

explanation.definitionFit: Judo grades are marked by coloured belts; and protected open land round towns is called by this name and described as a lung.

clue.text: Grind away with good 27

parts.note: the answer to 27 is a designer, and John Nash was a famous one

explanation.surface: Grind on, with a good designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 points to the answer of 27 across, so here John Nash, the Regency architect of London's terraces.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind the teeth together, so grind is a synonym.
